home: Open-source Rust software modem for amateur radio. Try the cross-platform preview and explore the bench-tested workflows for direct mail and terminal chat.
Use connected chat, file transfer, shared station certificates, and printable QSL cards in builds that enable the required features.
downloads: Verify the package SHA-256 before installing.
A complete public preview is pending. Follow
mail: Two Linkwise stations can exchange queued messages directly over the modem using Open B2F. A shared PKI profile enables signing and optional encryption.
The virtual BW500 bench checked attachment SHA-256 and clean disconnection. Separate P2P tests used Pat and Winlink Express.
The preview downloads contain the modem. SMTP, IMAP, and protected mail need their respective build and configuration. Gateway access and physical RF qualification are separate.
winlink: Winlink Express 1.8.6.0 received a 64-byte attachment from Pat through the Windows ARM64 Linkwise service. The SHA-256 matched and both peers disconnected cleanly.
Install Linkwise for Windows and open Configure Linkwise for Winlink. Enter the callsign you use in Express.
Select Radio-free waveform test and the BW500 measurement profile. Connect an isolated waveform peer to the port shown by the wizard.
In Express, go to VARA HF P2P → Settings → TNC Setup. Use 127.0.0.1 and command port 8300, or the custom port shown in the wizard. DATA uses the next port.
Select 500 Hz, disable Automatically launch TNC when session is opened, and reopen the session. Express displays VARA TNC as the selected session type.
Run Get-Service LinkwiseModem and confirm Ready and the loopback port in Express. Send a test attachment, compare SHA-256, and check both disconnect logs.
This test covers radio-free P2P attachment exchange. Physical RF and gateway operation require separate qualification.
guide: Operate a BW500 station, exchange public certificates, and reproduce the protected chat and mail workflows on an isolated link.
Validate the station JSON, audio devices, and BW500 measurement profile. Start the daemon and chat in separate terminals, using the same callsign as the station configuration.

Use one direct peer per call. /who and /status show the peer and link. Windows retain drafts and wrap at the current terminal width. Presence shows join, leave, disconnect and timeout. With shared PKI, |V is signed plaintext, |E is encrypted and verified, |X is verification failure, and |F is encryption or decryption failure. Both peers enter /encrypt to upgrade an active call. /proof exports the latest verified message.

Use the secure-transfer build for gzip and SHA-256. Plain file transfer is limited to 32 KiB. The receiver must accept the offer; the CLI never overwrites the destination. Stock VarAC MD5 file offers are declined. For encrypted files, use --secure-config and pair /receivefile --encrypt with /sendfile --encrypt in a dedicated mutually authenticated TLS 1.3 session.

Configure trusted CAs, current CRLs and per-callsign CA pins where multiple CA keys are trusted. Verify full SHA-256 fingerprints out of band before accepting certificates. Signed chat uses ECDSA P-256. Chat can use TLS 1.3 with ephemeral P-256, or require P-256 + ML-KEM-768 with the pqc-chat build and the approved OpenSSL FIPS provider configuration on both peers.

Generate a vector PDF carrying public certificates. Print at 100% on the blank side of a 5½ × 3½ inch stamped card, or use --size 4x6. Start qsl receive with verified fingerprints, then share a JPEG or PNG photo to the watched directory. Linkwise validates the offer and adds the peer to the shared profile.

Import and export with the same PKI profile. Add --encrypt to seal outgoing mail or require protected input on export. Use mail exchange and mail listen to carry the sealed B2F envelope. The encryption certificate is for store-and-forward mail; the signing certificate authenticates live chat.

Feed 48 kHz mono signed 16-bit little-endian PCM into receive-pcm, including a continuous KiwiSDR feed. It reports CRC-valid BW500 frames as JSON. Passive conversation reconstruction requires session reassembly. The connected chat client uses the modem DATA socket.

Bench and receive-only results have their stated scope. Use encryption only on an authorized transport. FIPS deployment requires the applicable validated module version, build and operating environment.
docs: Select a reference or switch languages. The catalog identifies documents with an English source and links to translated editions where available.
man: Use --check-config to validate JSON and --check-station to check audio and ports without playback. --serve-station runs native audio and binds the host sockets to IPv4 loopback. --serve-virtual-bw500 and --serve-virtual-wide provide radio-free waveform sockets.

Use UTF-8 JSON with version 1, callsign, and input and output device objects. Device channels are zero-based. Set bandwidth to 500, 2300, or 2750 for two-way audio. The default command and DATA ports are 8300 and 8301; BW500 two-way operation needs bw500_profile.
